metadata.title: How to Make Evaporated Milk | Bold Baking Basics
metadata.description:
Skip the store and make your own Evaporated Milk in 25 minutes!
Get the WRITTEN RECIPE here: http://bit.ly/EvapMilk
SUBSCRIBE HERE: http://bit.ly/GemmasBoldBakers

RELATED VIDEOS & RECIPES
*  Condensed Milk Recipe: http://bit.ly/GemsCondensedMilk
*  Dairy-Free Condensed Milk Recipe: http://bit.ly/CoconutCondensed

Hi Bold Bakers! My method for How to Make Evaporated Milk is so easy. I get so many requests for what to replace this ingredient with, or where to find it, and now you never have to worry about that — because evaporated milk can be made so easily at home in just 25 minutes! So let’s get baking!
 
ABOUT GEMMA
Hi Bold Bakers! I’m Gemma Stafford, a professional chef originally from Ireland, and I’m passionate about sharing my years of baking experience to show you how to bake with confidence anytime, anywhere! Join millions of other Bold Bakers in the community for new videos at 8:30am Pacific Time every Thursday and Sunday!

FOLLOW ME HERE, BOLD BAKERS!

* Facebook: https://www.Facebook.com/BiggerBolderBaking
* Instagram: https://instagram.com/gemma_stafford/
* Pinterest: https://www.pinterest.com/BiggerBolderBaking

The video is a cooking tutorial on evaporated milk. At the start, a person uses a spoon to scoop evaporated milk from a pot and then we see a shot of evaporated milk inside a measuring cup and a glass mug with milk in it.

summary.brief: Gemma simmers full‑fat milk, reduces it to a thick creamy liquid, strains it, and shows the finished evaporated milk in a jug and a glass mug.
summary.detailed: The video opens with music and Gemma greeting viewers in a bright kitchen. She pours a measured amount of full‑fat milk from a measuring cup into a non‑stick saucepan, places the pan on a burner set to medium heat and brings the milk to a gentle simmer. She then lowers the flame to medium‑low and lets the milk simmer quietly for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally with a red spatula to keep it from scorching. As the water evaporates, the milk darkens slightly and reduces to about 12 oz, taking on a creamy off‑white color. When the reduction is complete, she turns off the heat, positions a fine‑mesh sieve over a jug, and slowly pours the thickened milk through to remove the thin surface film. Finally, she holds up the jug and a glass mug to display the smooth evaporated milk, mentions its shelf life, and suggests using it in recipes such as chocolate rice pudding before thanking the audience and directing them to her website for the written recipe.

action.detailed: Simmer full‑fat milk in a non‑stick saucepan over medium‑low heat while stirring occasionally, then strain the reduced milk through a sieve into a jug to remove the surface film.
action.actor: Gemma Stafford, the presenter

The strained, creamy evaporated milk is shown in a measuring cup as she continues talking about its uses, storage (keeps about a week in the fridge), and how it can substitute for store‑bought evaporated milk in recipes.
